lines.en: I tap on Tsukasa’s name in my phone and wait for her to answer.
: ...Hello?
And I hang up the second she does because I am better than this.
Just because Tsubasa gave me her daughter’s number doesn’t mean I have to call her. And I’m not about to give into whatever subconscious temptation compelled me to do so.
She doesn’t need a tutor. And she definitely doesn’t need me as a tutor to top that off and put her in danger.
Which is what I am. Danger.
To her. To myself. To her family. To everyone around me. And I’ve reluctantly accepted how that won’t ever change.
But just because I am completely, irreparably broken doesn’t mean I should drag someone else into this mess lest the cycle continues.
I slide my phone back into my pocket. She doesn’t need to know it was me that called.
And I spend the rest of the afternoon thinking of how things could have gone wrong if I’d done something differently.
How they still could.
And how I’ll be running from this part of me forever with a ghost who feels more like a shadow right there behind me.
Fragments of a thread get caught in your teeth and you spit them out onto the concrete.
You are a disappointment and a failure.
: Hellooooo? You’ve reached the great and powerful Tsukasa Tsukioka. Speak now or I will have this number traced by my team of super hackers!
: Hey.
: Jeeves? Is that you?
: I guess so.
: How did you get my number? It’s supposed to be top secret. Even Nee-sama doesn’t have it.
: But Chinami does?
: Chinami is a business partner who I need to have important business conversations with. But you’re not a partner at all, Jeeves. You’re just a peasant. A peasant who steals phone numbers.
: Your mom gave it to me in the event that I decide to start tutoring again.
: Hmm...I’m not sure if I trust you as a tutor anymore, Jeeves. Your methods seemed quite counterintuitive at our last meeting.
: I wasn’t in the right frame of mind during our last meeting.
: Oh. Are you saying that you are in the right frame of mind today?
: No.
: Oh.

: In fact, I’m clearly insane for even calling you right now given how the conversation about doing this went with your mother. And you should hang up the phone immediately if you care at all about your future.
: Everybody else is so boring, though. At least you’re entertaining in a pitiful sort of way.
: I don’t need your pity, but I’ll accept it if I’ve already stooped this low.
: So, what do you want, Jeeves? Is it money? Or...have you done something unspeakable and you require my assistance disposing of the body? Or bodies. How many people have you killed?
: I’d rather not talk about that.
: That many? I’ll send my best men right away. Never fear, Jeeves. Your secret is safe with me.
: Tsukasa...I just...
: I wanted to know if you’re...
: If you’re free right now.
: As in...you actually have decided to take me on as a pupil? Even while Nee-sama is currently going uneducated?
: Touka’s in good hands with someone I trust to...do a much better job than I ever could.
: And while I haven’t exactly decided to start tutoring again...I think I need to meet with you and figure out if I’ll even be able to.
: Ah! Yes, I’m quite familiar with interviews like this.
: Please come now so I can determine whether or not I will accept you as the man in charge of my education. But do know that I’ve made many a grown man cry during my interviews.
: Oh, and dress nicely. You do want to make a good impression- don’t you, Jeeves? Especially if you are about to cry.
: This...isn’t really the type of meeting I had in mind considering you seemed more than willing to just hand me the job up until today.
: I think this is plenty considering how badly you botched your first attempt at teaching me anything.
: Your interview starts in ten minutes! Tardiness will not be excused.
: Tsukasa, I can’t teleport.
: Wow. You peasants really do have it rough.
: How about this, Jeeves? Close your eyes and think very hard about where you want to be.
: Uhh...okay.
: Now what?
: Open them, of course!
: That’s not going to work.
: You’re going to be a terrible tutor if you can’t listen to simple orders like this, Jeeves.
: Tsukasa, that’s-
: Wait. How the fuck?
: Behold the powers of ancient wizardry and infinite wealth! Now, bow down and kiss my foot, for you have entered my domain and must now do my bidding!
: Yeah, I’m not going to do that.
: You are refusing my command?
: Yes. Now, tell me how you teleported me here.
: You teleported yourself here, Jeeves. With the help of your imagination. Anything is possible if you try hard and believe in yourself.
: No...you did this.
: Yes, you’re right. I suppose I did. But I’ll be keeping the source of my powers a secret until after we’re wed. Only then will I let you in on my ancient magic.
: This is one of the least believable situations I’ve ever found myself in and I can talk to animals.
: Perhaps you’re an ancient wizard too, then? I had a feeling you were concealing hidden powers, Jeeves. You’ve passed the first test. But now, you must defeat my four henchmen.
: You’re going to...make me fight the dudes standing behind you?
: Of course. It only makes sense for my tutor to be able to protect me. And you never know when you’ll have to fight off a swarm of bad guys who want to kidnap me for nefarious purposes.
: No thanks.
: Jeeves? What are you doing?
: Teleporting myself back home. Anything is possible if you try hard and believe in yourself.
: Not so fast, commoner!
: I did not free up my extremely busy schedule to be toyed with by my interviewee.
: And I didn’t swallow the last bit of my pride to come here and fight a bunch of silent, menacing guards.
: What does your pride have to do with anything? You should be thankful to be in the presence of such power and influence. Most would jump at the chance to kiss my feet.
: Yeah, well, if I tell you what I meant by that, I’ll have to fight your henchmen whether I want to or not.
: Now I’m confused. Are you here to kidnap me for nefarious purposes? Because it would be much easier for me to just give you whatever you’re in search of rather than ransoming me for it.
: Tsukasa...I don’t know what I’m in search of. I don’t know why I’m here.
: It could be confronting a part of myself I don’t want to face or...honestly, maybe just because I see promise in you or something.
: Or hey, maybe I’m just so bad at socializing that I feel more comfortable around people who are still as mentally immature as you.
: Are you insulting me, Jeeves?
: Not intentionally. But yeah, probably. To a certain extent.
: I should teleport your innards across the Pacific Ocean to make you pay for such a thing.
: Honestly, I’d probably prefer that over this.
: You sure are weird, Jeeves. But it’s that weirdness that makes me want to hire you in the first place. And also the fact that it would make Nee-sama jealous.
: Interview complete! You’ve got the job!
: I don’t even know if I want it. Remember? That’s why I’m here in the first place.
: That’s why you came here! But now, you’re here for a different reason! To teach me things that many others have failed to teach me! While also keeping me entertained!
: But also, I’m legally obligated to inform you that you may be executed if you fail to live up to my expectations.
: Don’t tempt me with a good time.
: That’s the spirit, Jeeves! Nothing shows off that commoner mentality better than the acceptance that you may quite literally work yourself to death!
: Where are you going?
: To my nearest bedroom, of course! You don’t expect me to study outside, do you?
: Can we maybe go somewhere less private?
: But I’ll get distracted if others are present. A quiet environment is conducive to better learning. Even if I am already a genius.
: Tsukasa-
: Silence, Jeeves! You’ve subjected yourself to my rule and must now do as I say or be forever banished from...everything!
Tsukasa scurries off into the manor as three of her four henchmen stick right to her tail.
The fourth one moves behind me and silently urges me to chase after her as best as I can.
He’s expressionless. Almost like a doll. And I don’t think it’s unwise of me to acknowledge that as a probability considering the family we’re dealing with right now.
In the several glances I’m able to spare over my shoulder, I don’t see him blink even once. But that makes me uncomfortable as I can’t tell what he’s thinking.
I just know that if I were lucky enough to be wearing the shoes that he is, I wouldn’t be looking favorably upon me.
And Tsukasa shouldn’t be doing that as well — but she’s so excited to peel off the wrapping paper covering Pandora’s box that she spares no skepticism whatsoever.
Then, before I know it, the two of us are locked inside a lion’s cage. But I’m the lion and she is the plucked and skinned carcass of a game-fowl.
: Welcome to the den of ultimate knowledge! Where countless fools have perished at the hands of Tsukasa Tsukioka and her...ultimate knowledge!
: Your bedroom is two stories?...
: This one is. But I’ve been collecting them since I was old enough to walk and will one day inherit all of Nee-sama’s as well. And she has one that’s five stories tall.
: That seems...completely unnecessary. And you should probably let your sister keep at least one bedroom.
: Why? She doesn’t even sleep here anymore. She’s always with her weird friend who likes chairs too much.
: Ah. I see you’ve met Yasu, then.
: Come, Jeeves! Look over here!
: Tsukasa-
: This way, this way!
I follow Tsukasa to the other side of the room, prompting her henchmen to follow us. But instead of feeling intimidated by their presence, I’m just thankful they’re here.
I doubt I’d do anything. At least...not purposely. But it’s good knowing that there’s a failsafe in place in the event that my mind decides to go haywire again.
Plus, it’ll allow me to keep my thoughts in order and actually be able to teach for once.
I still know how to do that, right?
Wait, what am I even supposed to be teaching her?
: Isn’t the view from here amazing, Jeeves? I bet the one from your tiny, peasant apartment isn’t even close.
: I have a house, you know.
: Sorry. You’re just so low on the totem pole that I normally imagine you sleeping inside of a large cardboard box.
: Hey! Do you want to see something cool?!
: You’re not going to take me to your sister’s five-story bedroom next, are you? This one is...more than sufficient for your first lesson.
: Oh, no. We don’t have to leave. I just wanted to show you a cool trick that Mother taught me. Watch.
: Was something supposed to-
: Cool, right?
: My servants have taken a vow of silence and can only communicate through hand gestures. Which is kind of like me knowing a second language when you stop and think about it.
: I’m still way behind the many languages that Mother knows. But I’m almost guaranteed to catch up at this rate. Don’t you think?
: Sure. Now show me the hand gesture that brings them back inside.
: Why? Won’t it be easier for the two of us to study in private?
: I’d just feel a lot more comfortable if they sat in and watched.
: Well, I wouldn’t. I get nervous and uncomfortable when I have to do things in front of other people.
: You didn’t have any problems sitting in on my class and I have way more students than you have henchmen.
: I have 143 henchmen.
: Why?
: Because seven of them “quit.”
: Tsukasa-
: Do you not want to be alone with me, Jeeves? Is it because I annoyed you when we were alone in your office?
: It’s not that...
: I promise to be good. I really do want to learn. And if I do anything to annoy you, all you have to do is raise your right hand and I’ll stop talking until you say it’s okay again.
: Race you upstairs!
: Please don’t...
: But that’s where all of my notebooks are!
: Then bring them down here...
: But I want you to meet my friends! Come on, come on!
I give into her excitement when I know I shouldn’t.
I follow her up the stairs when I know I shouldn’t.
And I sit beside her on the bed when I know I shouldn’t.
: The cat is named Trixie. The bear is named Barry. The chicken is named Super Sonic Jalapeno Meltdown Catastrophe Nine-
: What?
: And the whale is named Franklin!
: Cool, right?
: ...Yeah. Yeah, they’re all really cool.
: So, what are we going to study today? Physics? Astronomy?
: Are those really the topics you want to study?
: I don’t really know. I’ve always had to follow a very strict regimen when it comes to my education. Mother says it’s the best way to properly exercise one’s brain.
: What I’m unsure of is how that regimen differs from that of the common man. But I imagine it’s quite a bit based on the gap in knowledge between Chinami and me.
: Yeah. It is. And, to be completely honest, I don’t know anything about physics.
: Astronomy then?
: Astronomy...makes me uncomfortable.
: Because of the black holes?
: Sure. Let’s go with that.
: Well, what topics are you interested in, Jeeves? There must be something considering your history in teaching, right?
: It’d be literature if anything.
: Then, do you want to talk about that book you mentioned the other day? The Catcher in the Rye?
: You...
: You read it?
: I didn’t have anything else to do when you left Chinami’s room. So I read the whole thing while she watched a strange television sponge.

: I particularly enjoyed the juxtaposition of the protagonist’s idealism with cynicism as it created an interesting dichotomy that paralleled how I often feel as an adventurous girl who must always obey the rules.
: You read the entire book in one sitting and came up with all of that by yourself?
: Did I misunderstand something? Was Holden Caulfield’s idealism naught more than a vessel to showcase hypocrisy in a believable, yet self-aggrandizing way?
: Jeeves?
: Akira?
: It’s “Sensei” while we’re here, Noriko.
: Do I really have to call you that? It feels super weird after calling you by your actual name for years.
: Just while we’re tutoring, okay? Now, tell me — what else did you find interesting about last night’s reading?
: Mostly just the progression of Holden’s feelings concerning simple matters like “youth” and “happiness” over time.

: It’s really easy for stories that focus on “coming of age” to come across as preachy and inauthentic but, despite how unbearable he was at times, Holden felt like a very realistic depiction of a teenager.
: Jeeves? Is your brain exploding again?
: Huh?
: You just...
: You reminded me of someone else just now.
: Nee-sama, perhaps? It was Mother who originally taught us literary analysis, so it’s quite possible my read on this book would echo that of my sister’s.
: I haven’t talked about this book with your sister. And I had no idea you were even going to read it.
: I had no idea we were going to talk about it. I was just bored.
: But now that I know what you’re interested in, you can teach me all sorts of things and we can both have fun! Right, Jeeves?!
: It’s “Sensei” while we’re here, Tsukasa.
And so the two of us remain on that bed.
UNTIL HER SMILE STARTS TO HAUNT ME AND OUR KNEECAPS TOUCH.
Something tells me I could fit a ring around her ankles and take back something I have lost with age.
